docRequirement: `fallbackModel` is a bounded ORDERED CHAIN, not a single model. `whats-new/index.md:54` reads in full: "Also this week: **sub-agents can spawn their own sub-agents** (background chains are capped at five levels deep); **`--safe-mode`** starts Claude Code with all customizations disabled for troubleshooting; and **`fallbackModel`** configures up to three fallback models tried in order." This index line binds exactly two properties of the key: arity (a list of up to three entries) and order (tried in sequence, so entry two is reached when entry one also fails). It is the Week-24 digest index, so it links `whats-new/2026-w24` and `model-config.md` for the rest of the semantics (turn-scoped switch, duplicate removal, `"default"` expansion, trigger class, comma-separated `--fallback-model`) — those are filed as f226/f106 and are deliberately NOT this spec's delta.
current: One model, one hop. Type: `packages/shared/src/config/config-defaults-schema.ts:51-52` declares `fallbackModel: string` with the docstring "Pi model ID to retry once after model/network drain errors. Empty disables fallback." — the word "once" is the contract we actually implement. Validation: `packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:135` is `fallbackModel: z.string()` inside `ConfigDefaultsSchema` (`validators.ts:105`), which `grep -arn ConfigDefaultsSchema` shows is referenced only by its own declaration and by `packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/validators-stored-config.test.ts:2` — test-only, so it is not the runtime gate. Load path: `packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:273-276` is `typeof defaults.workspaceDefaults?.fallbackModel === 'string' ? defaults.workspaceDefaults.fallbackModel.trim() : ''`, so a doc-shaped array on disk collapses to `''`; the in-code default is `fallbackModel: ''` at `storage.ts:194` and the shipped asset is `"fallbackModel": ""` at `apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json:28`. Read: `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6256-6258` `getFallbackModel(): string` returns `normalizePiFallbackModelId(loadConfigDefaults().workspaceDefaults.fallbackModel)`, and `packages/shared/src/config/models-pi.ts:20-22` is a bare `typeof modelId === 'string' ? modelId.trim() : ''` — no comma split, no array handling, no dedupe, no cap. Walk depth: `pi-agent.ts:444-446` `PiChatOptions` carries a boolean `fallbackModelRetry?`; `pi-agent.ts:6313-6324` `getRetryFallbackModel` returns null the moment `options?.fallbackModelRetry` is set (:6314) or when the single id equals the current model (:6319); `pi-agent.ts:6326-6344` `retryWithFallbackModel` calls `this.setModel(fallbackModel)` (:6335), yields the `info` notice (:6336-6339) and re-enters `chatImpl` with `fallbackModelRetry: true` (:6340-6343). Both live call sites pass `piOptions` through — the event-loop path `pi-agent.ts:6754-6761` and the catch path `pi-agent.ts:6795-6801` — so the second failure falls through to `emitStopFailureHookOnce` + `typed_error` + `complete`. Trigger set is `FALLBACK_MODEL_RETRY_ERROR_CODES` at `pi-agent.ts:337-344`. The one-hop ceiling is codified as intended behaviour by `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-fallback-model.test.ts:85-106` (single `info` event, exactly two `prompt` messages) and by the stub at `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-max-turns.test.ts:264-265`, which returns `null` as soon as `options?.fallbackModelRetry` is true. Backend scope: `grep -acn fallbackModel packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts` returns 0, so the key is Pi-only.
divergence: The key NAME and the scalar's VALUE format are right; the arity and the walk depth are wrong. (1) Arity: the type is `string`, not a list of up to three — and the failure is silent, because `storage.ts:273-276` coerces a doc-shaped `["a","b","c"]` to `''`, i.e. an array written per the page DISABLES fallback instead of configuring it. There is no comma-separated scalar path either (`models-pi.ts:20-22` only trims). (2) Order: there is nothing to order — the `fallbackModelRetry` boolean guard at `pi-agent.ts:6314` caps the walk at exactly one hop, so even if entries two and three existed they would be unreachable; "tried in order" needs a cursor (which entry did we already try) where we have a boolean (did we retry at all). (3) There is no three-entry cap because there is no list to cap. Everything else the index line mentions is a different finding: the turn-scope of the switch, duplicate removal, `"default"` expansion and the trigger class come from the linked `model-config.md` and are filed as f226/f106, and the `--safe-mode` and nested-sub-agent clauses of the same sentence are separate findings entirely.

change.what: Widen to `fallbackModel: string | string[]` — the legacy scalar must keep parsing forever, since `""` is already on disk in every existing install. Rewrite the docstring: an ordered chain of up to three Pi model IDs tried in sequence; empty string or empty array disables fallback. Deliberately keep the accepted-on-read type wide and let the load path narrow it, rather than making the on-disk shape array-only.

Add `normalizePiFallbackModelChain(raw: unknown): string[]` next to it: accept a string (split on `,`) or a `string[]`, trim each entry, drop empties, dedupe preserving first occurrence, then `.slice(0, 3)`. Anything else returns `[]`. Keep `normalizePiFallbackModelId` as a thin `chain[0] ?? ''` wrapper so nothing else has to change to compile. This function is where the page's "up to three" cap lives and is the natural unit-test target — it is pure and has no Pi SDK dependency, so the test does not need the subprocess.

Replace the string-only coercion with `normalizePiFallbackModelChain(...)` and store the normalized `string[]`. NOTE the import direction: `models-pi.ts` pulls in `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat` and its own header forbids renderer-reachable imports, and `storage.ts` is imported broadly — so put the pure normalizer in a leaf module (e.g. `packages/shared/src/config/fallback-model-chain.ts`) and re-export it from `models-pi.ts`, rather than importing `models-pi.ts` from `storage.ts`. This is a PERSISTED-shape change: the read path must never throw on the old scalar. `FALLBACK_CONFIG_DEFAULTS` at :194 becomes `fallbackModel: []`.

One line: `fallbackModel: z.union([z.string(), z.array(z.string())])`. Cosmetic-but-required for the test suite to keep passing; this schema has no runtime reader (only validators-stored-config.test.ts), so it proves nothing on its own — the storage.ts normalizer is the real gate.

Turn the boolean into a cursor. Replace `fallbackModelRetry?: boolean` with `fallbackChainIndex?: number` in `PiChatOptions`. `getFallbackModel()` returns `string[]` via the chain normalizer. `getRetryFallbackModel` keeps the `FALLBACK_MODEL_RETRY_ERROR_CODES.has(error.code)` guard, then walks forward from `(options?.fallbackChainIndex ?? -1) + 1`, skipping entries equal to `this.getModel()` (the existing :6319 self-check, now per-entry), and returns `{ modelId, index } | null` — null only when the chain is exhausted, which preserves today's terminal `typed_error` + `StopFailure` behaviour at both call sites. `retryWithFallbackModel` takes the index and forwards `fallbackChainIndex` instead of `fallbackModelRetry: true` (:6342). The two call sites at :6755-6757 and :6795-6798 need only the destructured shape updated. Recursion depth is bounded by the 3-entry cap, so no extra loop guard is needed. Do NOT change `setModel` semantics or the trigger set here — turn-scope and trigger class are f226's delta, and mixing them in makes this diff unreviewable.

blastRadius: Crosses a PERSISTENCE boundary, which is an explicit risk trigger in this repo: `fallbackModel` lives in `~/.nessy-agent/config-defaults.json`, written by `syncConfigDefaults` (packages/shared/src/config/storage.ts:200-227) from `apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json:28` and read by `loadConfigDefaults` (storage.ts:233-281) on every Pi turn via `pi-agent.ts:6257`. Widening `string` → `string | string[]` edits the `ConfigDefaults` interface in `packages/shared/src/config/config-defaults-schema.ts`, a type re-exported from the shared package, so every `workspaceDefaults` reader typechecks against it — and the read path must tolerate the old scalar indefinitely because it is already on disk. Type-level fallout to fix in the same change: `packages/shared/src/config/validators.ts:135`, `packages/shared/src/config/__tests__/validators-stored-config.test.ts:176,189,195,201,207`, `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-fallback-model.test.ts:76` (stubs `getFallbackModel` with a scalar), `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/pi-agent-max-turns.test.ts:264-265` (stubs `getRetryFallbackModel` with the `fallbackModelRetry` option name — renaming it breaks that suite). Runtime fallout: each extra hop replays `retryWithFallbackModel`'s `this.setModel(...)`, which forwards a `set_model` message into the live Pi subprocess over the JSONL wire and emits a `ConfigChange` automation event, so a three-hop turn triples both — anything matching on `config_keys: ['model']` sees the extra events, and the renderer's model indicator is written from that same path. `apps/electron/dist/resources/config-defaults.json` is a build output carrying the same value and regenerates. Import hygiene is a real constraint here: `packages/shared/src/config/models-pi.ts:1-14` forbids renderer-reachable importers because it pulls `@earendil-works/pi-ai/compat`, so the normalizer must not be imported into `storage.ts` from that module. No imported-plugin path, no MCP surface, no `apps/cli` flag reads this key (`grep -arn 'fallback-model\|fallbackModel' apps/cli/src` is empty). The Claude backend is untouched: `grep -acn fallbackModel packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts` is 0.
userImpact: None observable in a stock build, and that is itself the interesting part. The shipped asset sets `"fallbackModel": ""` (apps/electron/resources/config-defaults.json:28) and `syncConfigDefaults` rewrites the user's copy from the bundle on every launch (storage.ts:200-227), so there is no surface — no UI, no IPC, no CLI flag — that can set the key durably, and an overloaded Pi model just ends the turn with a typed error. What makes it surface: an admin or a developer bundling a value. Do it the way this page describes — an array of up to three models — and `storage.ts:273-276` silently coerces it to `''`: no fallback, no warning, no validation error, a config that looks accepted and does nothing. Do it with a single scalar and one drain error is survived, but a second one in the same turn is not — the user sees `Retrying with fallback model …` once, then a hard typed error, where Claude would have moved on to the second and third entries. Both are invisible until the primary model is actually degraded.
